To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
uranium in the form of U3O8-bearing residues is cleared from the rat lung with a clearance half-time of 1.4 days.

1) the U3O8 residue is a poorly absorbed material, 2) the lung burden of U3O8 is cleared from the lung by mucociliary clearance at a rate of 0.1% of the initial burden per day, 3) the U3 O8 residue is not a bioavailable material and 4) the U3 0 8 residue does not have any adverse effect on the lung.

(1) the lung retention of the U3O8 residue in rats was 0.1-0.5% of the inhaled dose, (2) 90% of the retained uranium was cleared from the lungs within 3 days, and (3) the lung retention and clearance of the residue were similar to those for other insoluble aerosols, including uranium dioxide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a biokinetic model for the prediction of the internal dose from inhalation of uranium octoxide.
the development of a model to predict the biokinetic behaviour in humans of uranium octoxide residues.
the development of a biokinetic model to predict the behaviour of uranium octaoxide (U3O8) bearing dust in the human body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the residue is of low toxicity.
, for the U3O8 residue, the lung burden is the most sensitive indicator of the internal exposure.
the biokinetic behaviour is not significantly different from that of the soluble form of U3O8.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the behaviour of uranium inhaled from the residue is very similar to that from the oxide, and that the behaviour is similar in rats to that in man.
the biokinetics of uranium in the human body can be predicted by combining the data from animal studies with data obtained from human studies.
the respiratory tract is a major target organ for the residue and that it is the most likely route of entry for the uranium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chest monitoring will not be sufficient to assess the internal dose of the U3O8 residue, but urinary excretion data can be used to confirm the absence of internal contamination.
the biokinetics of UO2 particles are different from those of UO3 particles, and that this difference is due to the different solubilities of these compounds.
the use of chest monitoring for assessing the internal exposure of uranium workers is not a new idea, and that it has been used for many years to assess exposure to radon daughters.
